hints: Focus on what each test tells you, starting with the most selective one for acids.
Effervescence with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ means X must contain a carboxylic acid group, $-\text{COOH}$, so rule out any structure without it.
Remaining orange with hot acidified dichromate means no group that can be oxidised, so check for primary or secondary alcohols and aldehydes and eliminate them.
walkthrough:
**Interpret the sodium carbonate test**

Effervescence with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3(s)$ gives off $\text{CO}_2$. Only a sufficiently strong organic acid does this.

$$\text{RCOOH} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{RCOONa} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This tells us X must be a carboxylic acid. Alcohols and aldehydes alone do not react.

**Interpret the sodium test**

Effervescence with $\text{Na}(s)$ gives off $\text{H}_2$ and shows an $\text{O-H}$ group is present.

$$\text{RCOOH} + \text{Na} \rightarrow \text{RCOONa} + \text{H}_2$$
This is consistent with a carboxylic acid, and also with alcohols, but we already know a $-\text{COOH}$ group must be present.

**Interpret the dichromate test**

Hot $\text{H}^+/\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ stays orange, so no oxidation occurs. It would turn green with a primary alcohol, secondary alcohol or aldehyde.

This means X cannot contain $-\text{CHO}$, $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ or $>\text{CHOH}$. Only tertiary alcohols, ketones and carboxylic acids resist oxidation.

**Apply to the structures**

We need a molecule with $-\text{COOH}$ but with no oxidisable alcohol or aldehyde. That is a carboxylic acid plus a tertiary alcohol, $>\text{C(OH)}$, which cannot be oxidised because there is no H on that carbon.

options.A: Contains $-\text{COOH}$ so it gives both effervescences, but it also contains a secondary alcohol, $\text{CH(OH)}$. This is oxidised by hot acidified dichromate to a ketone, so the solution would turn green, not stay orange.
options.B: Contains an aldehyde, $-\text{CHO}$, and a secondary alcohol. It has no carboxylic acid, so it would not give $\text{CO}_2$ with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$. Both the aldehyde and secondary alcohol would also be oxidised, turning dichromate green.
options.C: Contains an aldehyde and a tertiary alcohol. It has no $-\text{COOH}$ group, so no effervescence with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$. The aldehyde would be oxidised to a carboxylic acid, so dichromate would turn green.
options.D: Contains a carboxylic acid, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C(OH)COOH}$, so it gives $\text{H}_2$ with Na and $\text{CO}_2$ with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$. The only alcohol present is tertiary, with no H on the C-OH carbon, so it cannot be oxidised and hot dichromate remains orange. This fits all three observations.
